coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Res. 14-2022 (mandatory TSS registration, RD$10,000 minimum wage, written contract, portal domesticas.mt.gob.do) was declared unconstitutional by the Tribunal Constitucional in June 2023 (El Dia, 14 Apr 2025). TSS registration under Res. 551-08 began 1 May 2023; only 732 workers registered by June 2023. Labour Minister still backs inclusion. Legal status of the duty is unclear, so the trigger is weak. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Dominican register of scrap buyers found. A Senate bill would create a national council and export licences for ferrous and non-ferrous scrap and used lead-acid batteries (BAPU); I could not confirm whether it passed. Customs scrap auctions are not a duty on dealers. Candidate C12 (unverified).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnshops (casas de empeño) are DGII-supervised non-financial obliged subjects under Ley 155-17 art. 2 num. 17; DGII technical consultation of Jan 2026 confirms. Nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Dealers in precious metals, stones and jewellery are DGII-supervised obliged subjects (Ley 155-17; Norma General 04-2018 or 05-2018, sources disagree; list updated by Aviso 28-25). Nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No INTRANT or other register for dismantlers or used-parts sellers found. Used parts imports are not prohibited (Dominican Today 2023). INTRANT's workshop-registration deadline (Ley 63-17, probably 2018, year unconfirmed) has passed. DGII Norma 04-10 covers insurer-liquidated vehicles and scrap. Candidate C8 (weak).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Searches returned nothing current on cattle movement permits or trader registration. Only a 1935 border-movement decree and the DGG contact details turned up. Result is unverifiable, not a negative. Candidate C13 (unverified).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: DIGEMAPS (Ministry of Health, Decree 82-15) and its meat unit inspect slaughter. A 2026 TVN report describes an illegal slaughterhouse seizure. Butcher permits are an old municipal framework. No filing duty found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Resolution 07-2015 of the Ministry of Agriculture created a honey residue monitoring programme, an export beekeeper register (RAEX) and an exporter list (LINEAM). Export-only and tiny. Candidate C9 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Registration of veterinary establishments and medicines falls under Ley 259-71 and Reglamento 521-06, run by the Division of Registro de Productos y Establecimientos Veterinarios (Sanidad Animal, Ministry of Agriculture). No periodic filing or e-portal confirmed. Candidate C7 (unverified).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No driller licence or abstraction-permit regime found. INDRHI drills wells for free in drought areas; an opinion column says permits are hard to obtain. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Ley 225-20 (solid waste) and Decreto 320-21 (regulation) exist. Amendments to Ley 225-20 passed the Senate in Jan 2025 and went back to the Chamber of Deputies; promulgation unconfirmed. I found no specific rule on septic or waste haulers' registration or manifests. Candidate C10 (unverified).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No search spent. Budget went to categories with live regulators. No Dominican lift or boiler inspection regime was surfaced by any other search.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Rural aqueduct associations (ASOCAR/ASOCARS, SNAR) exist within INAPA's scheme. No regulation, fee or reporting duty found; Senate bills on sector reform and decentralisation are of unknown status. Candidate C11 (unverified).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Ley 311 of 1968; the Division of Pesticide Registration (Sanidad Vegetal) registers companies as representative, distributor, formulator, retail outlet or fumigator. IDB-funded post-registration inspectors audit outlets and depots. A Dec 2025 GEF document says there is no official updated list of authorised or banned products. Applicator licence not confirmed. Candidate C6.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: The Ministry of Labour's Dirección General de Empleo keeps a Registro Nacional de Agencias de Empleo. The 2022 draft resolution on agency rules was only a public consultation; a 25 Aug 2026 Revista Mercado article still treats it as unconfirmed. The PEI 2025-2028 lists agency regulation as a goal. Candidate C4 (weak, trigger not yet in force).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Asefuse says 80% of funeral homes are irregular and only about 40 private ones are legal (Apr 2025). The bill is still pending and no new law was found as of Aug 2026. The Ministry of Health issues permits. The Liga Municipal Dominicana published voluntary standards in 2023. Santo Domingo Este approved a private cemetery in Mar 2026. Candidate C3 (weak, no trigger).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ley 122-05 (art. 51) requires an annual ISFL-01 return to DGII within 120 days of year end, with donor list, expense detail by programme, member list and basic statements. Monthly 606/607, IR-3, IR-17 and TSS also apply where relevant. CASFL qualification is renewed every 3 years for associations that receive state or donor funds. CASFL holds more than 8,000 ASFL, roughly half active. Ley 30-26 (June 2026) sets a 3% monthly late surcharge, capped at 100%. No dedicated ASFL software found, but that search was weak. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Ley 63-17 gives INTRANT licensing of operators. Freight companies must register as cargo operators on INTRANT's platform to request special circulation permits (Res. 011-2025, holiday restrictions). INTRANT issued 50 passenger operation licences in Q1 2026 against a plan of 11; in 2024 it reached only 20.83% of target, held up by incomplete files. Disputes between Conatra and Fenatrano over routes continue. Decreto 5-19 covers vehicle technical inspection. Candidates C5 and C14.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Exchange agents and remittance firms are supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos under Ley 183-02; only 5 remittance agents operate. The SB closed 56 unauthorised agents in the past, and informal exchange houses persist. SB logged 153 infractions in H1 2026. Nothing found on street vendors or a micro-trader register. Candidate C15 (weak).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools need INTRANT/ENEVIAL accreditation, rolling out from Gran Santo Domingo (Ley 63-17); no deadline found. INAIPI runs public nurseries; no private nursery licence rule found. DIGEMAPS issued 11,826 registros sanitarios in 2024 (Decreto 528-01). Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters not searched. Candidates C16 and C17.

candidates.trigger: MICM Plan de Regularización de Estaciones since Aug 2016; Decreto 2119-72 art. 37 bans LPG filling at conventional stations; a 200 m separation rule was quoted by the minister.
candidates.unchecked: Dates of these sources (old), any current periodic report, whether the buyers are reachable and have budget.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Only old MICM material found: Plan de Regularización de Estaciones (since Aug 2016), GLP cannot be sold at conventional fuel stations (Decreto 2119-72 art. 37), and informal GLP stations. No current recurring report found. https://micm.gob.do/transparencia/images/pdf/publicaciones/libros/comunicados/Comunicado_MICM_estaciones_mixtas.pdf. Nothing new beyond weak lead C06.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Cocoa EUDR traceability and the Cacao Trace project (JAD/CODESPA/EU, 700 smallholders, 7 associations in Monte Plata) and the planned Cacao Dominicano geographic indication (2027) fall under K03. Nothing found for a coffee or INDOCAFE exporter register. Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: IDECOOP supervises co-operatives, but no mandatory periodic report or 2026 rule was found in two searches (only IDECOOP planning documents). Unverified; the IDECOOP site and its resolutions were not opened.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: MSP closed 501 health and aesthetic establishments from 2024 to April 2026 (281 in 2024, 177 in 2025, 43 to Apr 2026). Many had no habilitación licence or an expired one. Only 52 of 235 closed since 2025 reopened. 3,151 centres are habilitados. Based on Ley 42-01. ARS billing is already K08, K12 and K14; the habilitación duty is different, see C02.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy controlled-drug reporting is K13 (DNCD Digital). DNCD supervises precursor chemicals under Ley 50-88, but no registration or periodic-report rule was found. Industrial chemicals sit with MIMARENA through the VUCE (Decreto 470-14), per a WTO listing. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: The private security law is still pending after 16+ years. ADESINC asked for it again in June 2026. The sector has more than 62,000 employees. The SVSP (under the Ministry of Defence) licenses firms. A sectoral minimum wage of RD$24,633 from 1 Feb 2026 is unverified (from a non-official salary site). No concrete recurring report found. Firearm licences for security firms are in C03.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The Dirección General de Minería works under Ley 146-71 and Reglamento 207-98 and registers rights in the Registro Público. No quarry annual report or regularization programme found. Construction work-permit renewal is K04. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Not searched separately because it is covered by K01 (DGII goAML for non-financial obligated subjects). Nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: MITUR proposed RENATUR, a mandatory national register of short-stay properties with a unique credential per property, a certificate shown in the property, and platforms given 60 days to delist unregistered listings. Consultation opened 26 May 2026. The 22 Jul start was suspended or withdrawn (sources conflict). Airbnb supports it but wants Congress to approve it. ADORECO objects. See C01.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Cocoa EUDR is K03. Fish exports need a CODOPESCA no-objection certificate (Ley 307-04, VUCE/SIGA), and fishery licences are in C06. Customs operator licensing is under Decreto 609-24 (C07). Nothing else new.

coverage.category: 31. Firearms licence holders and weapons dealers (Ley 631-16; MIP resolutions 2024-2025)
coverage.found: MIP gave a fee-surcharge grace for overdue renewals through 31 Jan 2026 (Resoluciones MIP-RR-0008-2025 and MIP-RR-0010-2025). No later extension found. A Senate reform to make licences last 2 years is not confirmed as enacted. Renewal and payment is online at mip.gob.do/servicios. See C03.

coverage.category: 32. Solid-waste generators and waste managers (Ley 225-20, Decreto 320-21, PLANGIR Decreto 302-25)
coverage.found: Management plans, traceability, logbooks (bitácoras), insurance and guarantees apply to some actors. Thresholds and deadlines for small firms were not found. See C04.

coverage.category: 33. Personal data protection reform (Ley 172-13 amendment bill under discussion May 2026)
coverage.found: Still a bill. No regulator and no database registry confirmed. See C05.

coverage.category: 34. Freight and passenger transport operators (Ley 63-17, INTRANT, Decreto 258-20 on cargo)
coverage.found: INTRANT, RNTT and Fenatrado signed a satellite monitoring agreement. GPS copies from more than 800 trucks go to a monitoring centre. No 2026 deadline found. See C08.

coverage.category: 35. Fisheries: fishers, boat owners and exporters (Ley 307-04, CODOPESCA resolutions 002-2024 and 003-2024)
coverage.found: Services include fishing, fishing-exploitation and commercialization licences and export no-objection. Fisher carnetización has started in places (Samaná). No 2026 deadline found. See C06.

coverage.category: 36. Environmental permits for small businesses (Ley 64-00, MIMARENA permitting)
coverage.found: MIMARENA issued more than 6,500 permits in 2025 against 658 in 2019. Categories A (licence), B (permit), C (constancia) and D (CRIM minimal-impact certificate) exist, with renewals handled as separate files. ICA deadlines and any MIPYME treatment not found. See C09.

coverage.category: 37. Customs operators and freight forwarders (Ley 168-21, Decreto 609-24, Reglamento 96-98)
coverage.found: Decreto 609-24 sets licensing for customs operators and excludes freight agents. Reglamento 96-98 requires a RD$1,000,000 bond for freight agents and consolidators. No new small-importer registration found. See C07.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Dominican periodic lift, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection regime surfaced in 8 searches (Spanish and English) plus 2 fetches. The only lift rule found is Decreto 361-15 (MOPC, Reglamento para el Diseño de Medios de Circulación Vertical en Edificaciones, repeals Decreto 84-11), a design and accessibility regulation. The search summaries show no periodic inspection, certification or registration duty. The two MOPC PDF fetches returned only a heading (no text), so the decree's articles were not read; whether it has a maintenance or inspection article is unverified. Reglamento 522-06 (occupational safety, Ministerio de Trabajo) is a general safety-programme rule. No boiler or pressure-vessel article was confirmed. INDOCAL's NORDOM standards are voluntary unless adopted as an RTD, and no RTD for lifts or pressure equipment surfaced. LPG: MICM licenses distribution and retail under Ley 37-17 as amended by Ley 10-21 and Decreto 307-01 (e.g. Resoluciones 029-2024, 239-2025, 003-2026), but no cylinder or tank periodic-inspection rule surfaced. That belongs to category 21, so it was not pursued. Lift maintenance is sold privately (OTIS representative TECNAS E.I.R.L.) and in public tenders (Aduanas, PGR). Nothing in the results shows a mandatory regulator-facing workflow, so there is no candidate. Residual gap: Decreto 361-15 full text, the Reglamento 522-06 articles and any Bomberos or ayuntamiento lift permits were not read.
